AggregationConceptInRequest.description: An array of `AggregationTermInRequest` objects representing the terms to be aggregated for a single aggregation, e.g. terms corresponding to `sexAtBirth` and `diagnosis`.

AggregationTermInRequest.description: An object representing an individual term to be aggregated, e.g. a term corresponding to `sexAtBirth` or `diagnosis`. The `id` property is required and identifies the term to be aggregated, while the `filters` and `splits` properties are optional modifiers of the aggregation term. Note: The request object does not specifiy the property or scope of the aggregation.

filters.description:
Optional list of filters to select specific values of the given property for aggregation, as a modifier of the aggregation term. For example, for an aggregation term of `diagnosis` filters could be used to specify a subset of diagnoses to be aggregated.
Notes:
* While using the prototype of filters in the filtering section, these
  filters are not chained by the logical AND operator but are applied as
  a set of values to be used for the aggregation (i.e. evaluated separately)
* The `scope` property from `filteringTerms` does not apply since the scope
  is defined through the aggregation term itself.
* For value binning use the `splits` property instead of filters.

id.description: The `id` of the aggregation term as provided by the beacon. It is used to select the aggregation term, _i.e._ usually corresponding to a property in the data model.

splits.description: Optional list of **sorted** splits to group values for ranges or bins when performing the aggregation. TODO: object definition OR make it plain values? TODO: Define types and/or couple them to property type

description:
Terms used to specify items to return in an aggregation data response. Terms
are provided through the beacon's `/aggregation_terms` endpoint and the `id`
values of those terms constitute the possible `id` values here. See also the
documentation for `AggregationTermInResponse.id` in `beaconAggregationTermsResults`.

Note: The request for aggregations is a list of lists of objects:
* The outer list level is the list of all aggregations ("concepts") resulting
  in a distribution of one or more dimensional aggregation results.
* The individual concepts have lists of 1 or more (but mostly 1 or 2)
  aggregation terms - corresponding to individual properties - which are
  evaluated together, e.g. "diagnoses (1) for sex at birth (2)".
title: Aggregation Terms
